cities.name: Dublin

interests.name: Riverside Walks 🌊
interests.description: The River Liffey splits Dublin in two and creates some of the city’s best walking paths. Bridges, quays, and waterfront cafés bring a calm urban rhythm to the area. The scenery shifts from historic to modern architecture as you walk along the river. It’s one of the easiest ways to feel Dublin’s atmosphere.

interests.name: Historic Streets 🎭
interests.description: Dublin’s historic streets are full of character, music, and centuries-old architecture. Temple Bar is famous for its lively vibe, colorful buildings, and artistic corners. Nearby lanes reveal bookshops, pubs, murals, and cultural institutions. It’s a playful, energetic part of the city that blends old and new.

interests.name: Parks & Nature 🌿
interests.description: Dublin offers beautiful green escapes right in the heart of the city. St. Stephen’s Green is full of ponds, flowers, and peaceful walking paths. Locals come here to relax, eat lunch, or escape from busy streets. It's an essential part of Dublin’s everyday life.

interests.name: Local Food Exploration 😋
interests.description: Dublin’s comfort food culture revolves around warm soups, potatoes, breads, and pastries. Veggie-friendly options are easy to find across the city. Small cafés and bistros serve homemade-style meals that feel hearty and cozy. This is simple, delicious Irish food that warms you up instantly.

interests.name: Art & Culture 🎨
interests.description: Dublin is rich in museums, galleries, theaters, and literary landmarks. The National Gallery and surrounding cultural district offer both classic and contemporary art. Music, street performances, and creative events happen throughout the year. It’s a great city for travelers who enjoy artsy, culturally vibrant places.

cities.local_food_tip: Irish veggie soups, potato dishes, soda bread, pastries, salads — simple, tasty, warm, and comforting.
cities.full_day: Morning: Walk along the River Liffey starting near the riverside paths. → Visit Dublin Castle (exterior). → Coffee in Temple Bar. Afternoon: See the courtyard of Trinity College (exterior). → Lunch: Irish veggie soups, potato dishes, salads. → Relax in St. Stephen's Green. Sunset: Enjoy golden-hour views at Samuel Beckett Bridge. Night: Riverside lights and dessert spots around the quays.

places.name: River Liffey Walk
places.description: The River Liffey walkway is a calm urban route lined with landmarks and bridges. It’s perfect for easy morning or sunset strolls. Visitors get a great sense of Dublin’s mix of modern and historic architecture.

places.name: Dublin Castle
places.description: Dublin Castle is a historic complex at the heart of the city. While the interiors require tickets, the exterior courtyards are open and atmospheric. The site blends medieval remnants with elegant Georgian buildings.

places.name: Temple Bar District
places.description: Temple Bar is Dublin’s colorful, lively cultural quarter. Famous for pubs, music, galleries, and narrow cobbled streets, it's a place full of energy. Perfect for café breaks, photos, and artistic vibes.

places.name: Trinity College
places.description: Ireland’s oldest university offers grand courtyards, old libraries, and a calm academic atmosphere. Even if you don’t enter the Book of Kells exhibit, the exterior alone feels historic and impressive.

places.name: St. Stephen’s Green
places.description: A beautiful Victorian park in central Dublin, full of ponds, bridges, statues, and quiet paths. Locals come here to relax, have lunch, or enjoy nature in the middle of the city.

places.name: Samuel Beckett Bridge
places.description: A modern harp-shaped bridge that has become one of Dublin’s iconic symbols. It’s especially stunning at sunset when the river reflects soft colors and lights.

hidden_gems.name: Iveagh Gardens
hidden_gems.description: A peaceful, lesser-known park hidden behind buildings near St. Stephen's Green. It features waterfalls, lawns, and quiet corners perfect for escaping crowds.

hidden_gems.name: Meeting House Square
hidden_gems.description: A cultural courtyard in Temple Bar known for outdoor screenings, art events, and its retractable canopy. It’s lively in the evenings yet still feels local.

ideas: Park blossoms throughout St. Stephen’s Green.
Outdoor coffee terraces in Temple Bar.
Long bright evenings across the riverfront.
Ice cream near Samuel Beckett Bridge.
Picnics in the city’s largest parks.
Orange and yellow tones in St. Stephen’s Green.
Christmas lights across the city center.
Hot chocolate cafés near Temple Bar.

public_transport_tips.tip: 🚊 Luas trams run through major parts of the center.
🚌 Dublin Bus covers the entire city.
🚶 Central Dublin is compact and easy to explore on foot.
📱 Use the TFI Live app for route planning.

city_events.name: Dublin Fringe Festival
city_events.description: Creative performances, theater acts, and artistic experiments across venues and outdoor spaces.

cities.name: Cork

interests.name: Riverside 🌊
interests.description: The River Lee flows through the heart of Cork, creating scenic walking paths and peaceful spots along both channels. Riverside cafés and bridges make it perfect for slow morning strolls. The reflections of colorful houses and historic warehouses add to the charm.

interests.name: Old Town 🎭
interests.description: Cork’s Old Town is full of lively streets, historical lanes, and traditional Irish atmosphere. Markets, shops, and old pubs define the character of this compact district. It’s the best place to feel Cork’s cultural rhythm.

interests.name: Food Culture 😋
interests.description: Cork is considered Ireland’s food capital, offering fresh local produce, bakeries, soups, and traditional Irish meals. The English Market is the center of the city’s culinary scene. Travelers can enjoy everything from warm vegetable stews to authentic pastries.

cities.local_food_tip: Veggie stews, breads, soups, potato dishes and pastries — simple, hearty, and comforting Irish flavors.
cities.full_day: Morning: Walk along the River Lee → explore St. Patrick's Street (exterior) → coffee in a local café. Afternoon: Enjoy a warm lunch (soups, breads, veggie meals) → visit the exterior of Crawford Art Gallery → relax in Fitzgerald Park. Sunset: Climb or view the Shandon Tower for city panoramas. Night: Riverside reflections and a calm evening walk.

places.name: River Lee Walks
places.description: The River Lee surrounds Cork’s center with scenic promenades, bridges, and peaceful waterside paths. Ideal for morning walks and photography.

places.name: St. Patrick's Street
places.description: Cork's main street, lined with shops, cafés, and historic buildings. It’s one of the liveliest areas in the city.

places.name: Crawford Art Gallery
places.description: A central cultural landmark with Irish art collections. Even viewing the exterior gives a sense of Cork’s artistic identity.

places.name: Fitzgerald Park
places.description: A lush riverside park featuring sculptures, a museum, and relaxing gardens. Perfect for breaks and slow afternoon walks.

places.name: Shandon Bells & Tower
places.description: One of Cork’s iconic landmarks. Climbing the tower reveals sweeping views across colorful neighborhoods and the River Lee.

places.name: English Market
places.description: A historic food market filled with local vendors, fresh produce, baked goods, and Irish specialties. A core of Cork’s food culture.

places.name: Elizabeth Fort
places.description: A 17th-century fort offering elevated views of Cork’s southern districts. Quiet, atmospheric, and full of history.

places.name: University College Cork (UCC)
places.description: Beautiful stone buildings, gardens, and river paths make UCC one of Ireland’s most picturesque campuses.

hidden_gems.name: Nano Nagle Place Gardens
hidden_gems.description: A peaceful heritage center with gardens, courtyards, and quiet spaces. It feels hidden despite being close to the city center.

hidden_gems.name: Cork Butter Museum Area
hidden_gems.description: A quirky historic corner in Shandon, with charming lanes and local character. Perfect for travelers who enjoy offbeat spots.

public_transport_tips.tip: 🚌 City buses cover the entire center and suburbs.
🚶 Cork’s old town is compact and easy to explore on foot.

city_events.name: Cork Jazz Festival
city_events.description: 🎷 One of Europe’s top jazz festivals, filling Cork with music and nightlife.

cities.name: Limerick

interests.name: Riverside 🌊
interests.description: The River Shannon flows directly through Limerick, forming wide scenic views and peaceful embankments. It's ideal for morning strolls and calm photography spots. The riverside captures the city’s quiet charm, especially at sunrise and sunset.

interests.name: Historic Streets 🎭
interests.description: Limerick’s Old Town features medieval lanes, traditional Irish facades, and colorful shopfronts. Walking here feels like stepping through centuries of history. It’s a lively area with cafés, markets, and character everywhere you look.

interests.name: Culture & Parks 🌿
interests.description: Limerick blends cultural spots and green escapes, offering art museums, historic squares, and peaceful parks. It’s a balanced city where you can switch from galleries to nature within minutes. Perfect for travelers who like variety.

cities.local_food_tip: Soups, breads, veggie dishes and pastries — warm, simple, traditional Irish comfort food.
cities.full_day: Morning: Walk along the River Shannon → admire King John's Castle (exterior) → coffee in a local café. Afternoon: Explore the city center → warm lunch (potato dishes & soups) → stroll past the Art Museum (exterior). Sunset: Watch the sky over the Shannon waterfront. Night: Quiet riverside walk with soft city lights.

places.name: King John’s Castle
places.description: A massive medieval fortress on the River Shannon. Its towers and walls dominate the skyline and offer rich history.

places.name: The Milk Market
places.description: A lively local market with food stalls, crafts, pastries, and Irish delicacies.

places.name: People’s Park
places.description: A green, elegant park with trees, flowers, and the iconic bandstand — perfect for relaxation.

places.name: St. Mary’s Cathedral
places.description: An impressive medieval cathedral with atmospheric stone interiors.

places.name: Arthurs Quay Park
places.description: A small city-center park with river views and peaceful seating.

places.name: Hunt Museum
places.description: A major cultural museum featuring medieval, Celtic, and European artworks.

places.name: Shannon Bridge
places.description: A perfect spot for photography with dramatic river views.

places.name: King’s Island District
places.description: Historic center of medieval Limerick, full of character and old architecture.

hidden_gems.name: Bishop’s Palace Garden
hidden_gems.description: A quiet historical garden tucked between old stone buildings — peaceful and atmospheric.

hidden_gems.name: Sarsfield Bridge Viewpoint
hidden_gems.description: A low-traffic viewpoint perfect for evening river reflections.

public_transport_tips.tip: 🚌 Local buses connect all main districts of Limerick.
🚶 The city center and riverside are best explored on foot.

cities.name: Waterford

interests.name: Historic Streets 🎭
interests.description: Waterford’s historic streets reflect more than 1,000 years of Irish and Viking heritage. The Viking Triangle is filled with medieval lanes, towers, and old stone buildings that give the city a unique old-world charm. Museums and cultural spaces bring history to life in a compact, walkable area. It’s ideal for travelers who love exploring authentic, atmospheric districts.

interests.name: Coastal Walks 🌊
interests.description: Waterford’s waterfront provides calming coastal paths with views of the harbor and the estuary. Gentle sea breezes and open spaces make it perfect for morning or sunset walks. The area blends maritime heritage with modern promenade vibes. Many cafés and restaurants line the waterfront, creating beautiful seaside moments.

interests.name: Urban Culture 🎨
interests.description: Waterford is famous for its large outdoor murals created during the Waterford Walls festival. Street art brightens the city with colorful characters, geometric shapes, and cultural themes. The murals are scattered across neighborhoods, turning ordinary walls into open-air galleries. Exploring them feels like a creative treasure hunt.

cities.local_food_tip: Veggie soups, Irish breads, salads and pastries — warm, simple, and perfect for seaside weather.
cities.full_day: Morning: Explore the historic Viking Triangle with its medieval streets and towers → enjoy a peaceful Waterfront walk → coffee in a local café. Afternoon: Follow the open-air mural trail of Waterford Walls → lunch with soups, breads, and warm Irish dishes → relax in city parks. Sunset: Harbor golden-hour views along the waterfront. Night: Old-town stroll with lights, cafés, and riverside reflections.

places.name: Viking Triangle
places.description: The cultural and historical core of Waterford, filled with narrow medieval streets and Viking fortifications. Visitors can explore towers, museums, and charming squares. It’s one of the most atmospheric areas in Ireland for history lovers.

places.name: Reginald's Tower
places.description: Ireland’s oldest civic building and a symbol of Waterford’s Viking heritage. Its round stone structure offers a striking visual along the waterfront. Inside, exhibitions highlight the city’s ancient past.

places.name: Waterford Crystal Visitor Centre
places.description: A world-famous crystal studio where artisans craft intricate glass pieces. Visitors can observe the production process and browse unique creations. It’s one of Waterford’s artistic highlights.

places.name: Waterfront Promenade
places.description: A modern riverside walkway with open views, cafés, and benches. Ideal for morning walks or sunset photography. The calm water and harbor atmosphere create a peaceful city experience.

places.name: Bishop’s Palace
places.description: A Georgian palace featuring local history from the 1700s onward. Its rooms display art, maps, and decorative treasures. The architecture alone makes it worth a visit.

places.name: Waterford Walls Murals
places.description: The city-wide mural project that transformed Waterford into an open-air gallery. Each piece is unique, colorful, and highly photogenic. Exploring them offers a modern, vibrant contrast to the historic streets.

places.name: People’s Park
places.description: A peaceful urban park with Victorian-era landscaping. Locals enjoy picnics, strolls, and quiet reading under large trees. It brings a relaxed escape into the heart of the city.

places.name: Quayside Harbor
places.description: A scenic harbor area perfect for leisurely walks and sunset moments. Boats, waterfront views, and the soft river light create a tranquil atmosphere.

hidden_gems.name: Viking Longboat Replica
hidden_gems.description: A reconstructed Viking longboat displayed near the waterfront. It’s a striking reminder of Waterford’s origins and a great photo stop away from the main crowds.

hidden_gems.name: Cathedral of the Most Holy Trinity Garden
hidden_gems.description: A quiet hidden garden entrance beside the cathedral, offering shade, benches, and a peaceful atmosphere. Perfect for an afternoon break during city exploration.

ideas: 🍦 Ice cream stops near the quays.
🌇 Long golden-evening light by the harbor.
🍁 Warm shades in parks and quiet streets.
🎄 Holiday lights throughout the old town.

public_transport_tips.tip: 🚌 Waterford city buses connect the center with suburbs and the quays.
🚆 Train connections to Dublin, Limerick, and other cities are available from Plunkett Station.
🚶 The Viking Triangle and waterfront areas are compact and ideal for walking.

city_events.name: Waterford Winterval
city_events.description: 🎄 Christmas festival with lights, markets, shows, and family events.
